HTML skill review

Architecture, visual fidelity, and product review of the html skill, plus a roadmap for turning it into a workhorse for anything HTML.

Verdict

The skill has unusually good editorial judgment and a thin, capable toolchain, but it is built as a document renderer with a veto list. It knows what bad HTML looks like and forbids it well. It does not yet make an agent fast, verifiable, or versatile. Three things hold it back: agents are told to read galleries built for human eyes, the render-verification harness it already owns is unplugged, and the boundaries turn away most of what people actually want from HTML: decks, dashboards, explorables, email, print.

Thesis. Keep the taste and make authoring code. A page is a small JavaScript program built from typed HTML helpers, composed for one specific output type, checked by one command that returns a picture the agent actually looks at, and carrying its own source for the next edit.

What to keep

  • The anti-slop editorial rules. No KPI theater, no invented numbers, no meta-narration, one accent, severity as text. These are the skill's moat and survive every proposal below.
  • DESIGN.md → theme.css compilation with a --check gate in verify.py. One source of truth for every token.
  • Self-describing registry fragments with when, variants, and gotchas headers, plus data-component anchors for later edits.
  • The page-set manifest, with hierarchy, cycle detection, atomic publish, and refusal to overwrite. Solid engineering.
  • Precise delivery states (standalone, linked set, published). This prevents false "it's live" claims.
  • The template contract (artifact-template.json), with how already using it. That makes HTML a platform for other skills, not just a skill.

Architecture findings

Today's agent path

Today the agent reads two instruction files, then is sent to 613 KB of human galleries, copies fragment markup by hand, names every component a second time, and delivers. The working render check sits beside the path with no link to it.

  1. High

    Dollar patterns in content corrupt the page

    Evidence. pageShell (assemble.mjs:94-101) and the page-set nav injection (:390-392) pass user text as the replacement string in String.replace. Reproduced: --title 'Cost $& more' renders <h1>Cost <h1>Document title</h1>amp; more</h1>. A body containing $' splices the shell's tail into the page.

    Consequence. Any shell snippet, price, or regex in a code panel can silently mangle a delivered page, and the current tests don't catch it.

    Action. Use replacer functions (() => value) everywhere and add a regression test. Also: chart.mjs --from-fragment rewrites the whole target file with only the chart (:197), so pointing it at a full page destroys the page.

  2. High

    Agents are routed through human galleries

    Evidence. authoring.md tells the agent to "open the finished-page examples" (outcomes/index.html, 420 KB with three base64 PNGs) and choose components "in the component atlas" (atlas.html, 193 KB). The agent-readable index, registry.json, is never named as the selection surface.

    Consequence. Every new page either burns a large share of context on raw HTML or skips the step silently. Either way, selection quality depends on luck.

    Agent-facing files by size, KB
    outcomes/index.html
    420
    atlas.html
    193
    all references + SKILL.md
    56
    diagrams.html
    36
    registry.json (not referenced)
    6

    Action. Split the surfaces. Agents select from registry.json and an assemble --show <name> skeleton. Galleries stay for humans and for screenshot-based taste checks.

  3. High

    The render-verification harness is unplugged

    Evidence. scripts/capture-artifact.mjs renders a delivered page across viewport, theme, motion, and JS states and fails on overflow. visual-check.mjs does the same for components and includes a contrast check. Their doc mentions were removed in 3910f6fe, and neither has a test. authoring.md instead says "Never run automated HTML structural validation."

    Consequence. Agents fall back to ad-hoc browser screenshots or none at all, even though the repo already owns a better check. The absolute prohibition reads as banning the harness too.

    Action. Promote capture-artifact into a documented verify step that emits a contact sheet. Reword the ban to target what it actually meant: W3C-style markup validators.

  4. Medium

    The assembler makes the agent say everything twice

    Evidence. Body fragments already carry data-component on every root, yet --components must list them again. A missing name ships an unstyled component with no warning. toc-rail requires the same links hand-written twice (wide and compact), although the assembler sees every <section id><h2>.

    Action. Infer components from the body, fail on unknown names, and generate the TOC from sections. That removes the two most common silent defects.

  5. Medium

    Geometry is hand-authored where agents are weakest

    Evidence. chart.mjs computes only bar and sparkline. The other sixteen diagram families in diagrams.html are copy-and-adapt inline SVG with fixed coordinates.

    Consequence. Coordinates are exactly what LLMs get wrong. The atlas's own flowchart already has edge labels colliding with connectors.

    Action. Generate the families that have a layout algorithm (flow, state, sequence, tree, swimlane, timeline, line, stacked, waterfall) from specs, the same way bars are generated today.

  6. Medium

    The working source is thrown away

    Evidence. "Keep the fragment temporary by default." Later edits fall back to component-level surgery on the compiled file, and only chart specs survive as comments.

    Action. Embed the body source and manifest in the output as an inert JSON block, so any delivered file can be rebuilt losslessly by the next agent.

  7. Medium

    Galleries are hand-maintained snapshots

    Evidence. theme.css is inlined verbatim into eight files, including two in how, and all eight match today. Nothing enforces that: generate-theme --check only compares theme.css to DESIGN.md. The atlas carries only 71 of sequence-nav's 135 CSS lines and has no demo of it. diagrams.html duplicates the atlas's diagram section.

    Action. Generate the atlas, diagram atlas, and outcome pages from registry fragments and specs, and add a staleness check beside the theme check.

  8. Low

    Guidance is spread across overlapping read paths

    Evidence. About 7,300 words across eight references. Width modes, TOC thresholds, and "don't invent controls" are each restated in two or three files. authoring.md alone is 2,000 words and is mandatory.

    Action. Keep one mandatory 600-word core loop. Move everything else behind the mode or component that needs it.

Visual fidelity

Rendered at 1280 px light and 375 px dark in the in-app browser: the outcome gallery, decision comparison, incident account, diagram atlas, and component atlas.

SurfaceVerdictDetail
Outcome pagesStrongCalm hierarchy, correct measure, good tabular numerals, clean dark mode, and stat tiles that reflow correctly at 375 px. Credible, if Vercel-docs-generic.
Diagram atlasWireframe gradeSVG text scales with the viewBox (16 px effective, larger than the 15 px body). Flowchart "yes/no" labels collide with their edges. The donut center reads a meaningless "100%". Gray panels nest inside cards, breaking DESIGN.md's own "no page-in-a-page" rule. Values are set in mono, against the mono rule.
Narrow diagramsAcceptableContained horizontal scroll, no page overflow. Wide boards crop instead of reflowing, which is honest but loses the right third at first read.
GalleriesMixedUseful at a glance, but full of the meta-narration the skill bans ("How to use this view", "See the first frame before reading the rules"). Agents copy what they see.
RangeNarrowOne type scale and one density for everything. A deck needs larger type and a dashboard a denser rhythm. Each output type should own its scale within the same tokens, not stretch the document scale.

Product review

The description spends as many words on what the skill refuses as on what it does. Three of its refusals route to places that do not exist:

  • "Use an interactive-visualization workflow" appears in SKILL.md, authoring.md, and the outcome registry. No such skill exists in either plugin.
  • "Do not use HTML for slides" has no alternative route at all, even though decks are one of the most common HTML requests.
  • Dashboards, email, print/PDF, and small explorables have no home. ui-design owns production UI, not a one-file dashboard for a weekly review.
Output people ask forTodayProposed kit
Report or explainerSupportedreport
Course or linked setSupportedreport set
Embeddable fragmentSupportedreport fragment
Static product mockSupportedreport + mockup helpers
Slide deckRefused, no routedeck
DashboardRefused, routed to a skill that doesn't existdashboard
Explorable or calculatorRefused, routed to a skill that doesn't existdashboard inputs, later
EmailNo guidanceemail
Print or PDFNo guidancereport print stylesheet

The result is a skill that says no to most of what "all things HTML" means, and a user who gets a refusal where they wanted an artifact. The restraint is right for documents. It is wrong as the skill's whole identity.

Dogfood run

This page was built with the skill's own assemble.mjs, from a body fragment, to feel the agent path directly.

  • Listing components separately from the markup that already names them was the first friction.
  • Writing nine TOC links twice was the second.
  • Choosing components meant reading raw fragment files, because the atlas is too large to load and registry.json has no markup skeletons.
  • There was no documented way to verify the render. capture-artifact.mjs had to be found by reading the scripts directory.
  • The $ bug from the first finding hit this page. Literal $& and $' in the review text were expanded and pushed half the page out of its column, until every dollar sign was escaped by hand.
  • Once found, it worked well: 11 states passed in 50 seconds. But it wrote eleven full-page PNGs (about 9 MB total, up to 11,700 px tall) that an agent cannot practically inspect. The harness proves layout safety. It does not give the agent a way to see the page.
  • The capture caught a real mistake (diagram labels at 9.5 px at 768 px). It also passed a full-page shot with a blank image and a hidden chart, and it overrode this page's pinned dark theme in its light states.

Pages as programs

Agents are fluent in HTML and JavaScript, so the page should stay HTML and the tooling should be code. A page becomes a small ES module that composes typed helper functions, reads its own data, builds itself, checks itself, and carries its own source. Raw HTML stays first-class through an escaping html`` template, so no new language sits between the agent and the markup.

status.page.mjs
import { report, section, finding, bars, callout, html } from "dots-html/report.mjs";
import { readJSON } from "dots-html/data.mjs";

const sizes = readJSON("./sizes.json");   // real data in, not pasted numbers

export default report({ title: "HTML skill review", context: "dots / html", layout: "wide" }, [
  section("verdict", "Verdict", [
    callout.note("Thesis.", "Keep the taste; make authoring code."),
  ]),
  section("architecture", "Architecture findings", [
    finding.high({
      title: "Dollar patterns corrupt the page",
      evidence: html`<code>pageShell</code> passes user text to <code>String.replace</code>.`,
      action: "Use replacer functions and add a regression test.",
    }),
    bars(sizes, { title: "Agent-facing files, KB", emphasis: "outcomes/index.html", source: "wc -c" }),
  ]),
]);

Running node status.page.mjs writes one self-contained HTML file. Only the CSS for helpers that were actually called is included, the TOC comes from the sections, the sources footer is collected from every source:, and the module is embedded so the page can be rebuilt later.

The build loop

The agent writes page.mjs against one kit and its real data, then runs it. check returns a contact sheet and JSON findings tied to helper call sites. The agent edits the program until the check is clean, then delivers.

What the helpers make possible

IdeaWhat it changesWhy agents win
Escaping html``Every interpolation is escaped unless it's already an html`` value. The $-pattern bug class, broken entities, and injected markup disappear.Raw HTML is still just HTML; there is nothing new to learn.
Component functionsfinding.high({...}), callout.warn(), table(rows, cols), section(id, title, kids), generated from the existing registry fragments with their CSS reused verbatim.Named arguments replace copied anatomy. No --components list and no hand-written TOC.
Contracts at call timeHelpers throw on rule breaks: a second recommendation(), an image without alt, a comparison grid whose count doesn't match its columns, a severity not in the allowed set, or more than two emphasized diagram nodes.The editorial rules become enforced code rather than 7,000 words to remember. Errors point at the line.
Provenance by defaultstat(), bars(), and line() require a source (or an explicit "illustrative"), and sources are gathered into the footer automatically."No invented numbers" becomes a build error, not a hope.
Data in, page outA page can read CSV, JSON, or command output directly. A weekly status report becomes node status.page.mjs against this week's data.Recurring artifacts stop being rewritten; they are rerun.
Figure helpers with layoutflow({nodes, edges}), state(), sequence(), timeline(), line(), and stacked() use deterministic layered layout, text measured against a width table, and labels that never drop below 11 px. svg`` remains for everything else.Agents describe the relationships; the code handles the coordinates they get wrong.
Round-trip sourceThe module and a snapshot of its data are embedded inert in the output, and dots-html extract page.html recovers them.Any later agent edits the program, not the compiled page.
Catalog from code--list and --help finding print a helper's signature and a minimal example from its JSDoc. registry.json, the atlas, and the diagram atlas are produced by rendering every example, and each example doubles as a visual test.The agent reads about 30 lines instead of 613 KB, and the galleries can't drift.

Kits, composed per output type

Each output type is its own kit, with its own shell, primitives, rules, and check profile. Kits share only the core (html``, tokens, escaping, check). The agent chooses the kit first and composes for that medium from the first line. Nothing converts one type into another.

KitIts own primitivesIts own rules and checks
reportToday's page components, page sets, and fragmentsMeasure, one recommendation, provenance, and a print stylesheet
deckslide(), title(), bigNumber(), build() steps, speaker notesOne idea per slide, a larger type scale, keyboard navigation, 16:9 print pages; the check fails on slide overflow
dashboardgrid(), panel(), sortable and filterable table(), series() toggles, state kept in the URLDense rhythm, every control complete with JS off, no KPI theater; the check runs each control
emailTable layout, button(), image-safe stat()Inlined CSS, no script, width of 600 px or less; the check renders in a client-safe profile

Roadmap

Each phase ships on its own and has a concrete way to show it worked. Phase 0 is a set of four correctness fixes to the tools that exist today, before anything new is built.

PhaseShipsProof it worked
0 · CorrectnessThe four PRs below: literal replacement, in-place chart edits, loud component mismatches, and a trustworthy captureRegression tests for each. A seeded blank image and an unrevealed chart now fail capture.
1 · Helper corehtml`` with escaping, the report kit with component functions generated from the 25 fragments, section() with an automatic TOC, and CSS by use. assemble.mjs becomes a thin wrapper, so body fragments still work.The four outcome pages are rebuilt as page.mjs and match their current screenshots within a pixel-diff threshold.
2 · Check loopcheck: capture plus lint (SVG label overlap, text under 11 px, contrast, external requests, overflow, undecoded images) and one contact sheet, required by SKILL.mdA fixture set with one seeded defect per rule, where every fixture fails and the clean page passes
3 · Contracts + provenanceCall-time validation for the editorial rules, a required source on quantitative helpers, and an automatic sources footerEach rule has a failing fixture whose error names the call site
4 · Figuresflow, state, sequence, timeline, line, stacked, and a diagram atlas regenerated from specscheck reports zero label overlaps from 320 to 1280 px, and the flowchart and donut defects are gone
5 · Catalog + round-trip--list and --help, galleries generated from helper examples, embedded source, and extractCI fails on gallery drift, and extract-then-rebuild is byte-identical
6 · Deck kitThe highest-demand refusal today, with its own outcome example and check profile. SKILL.md drops "do not use HTML for slides".Golden tasks (outline to deck, doc to talk) pass a screenshot rubric, and print to PDF paginates cleanly
7 · Dashboard kitDense grid, table controls, URL state. The route to the nonexistent interactive-visualization workflow is removed.Golden tasks (CSV to weekly dashboard) pass, and check operates every control with JS on and off
8 · EvalsTen fixed golden tasks across kits, rendered and scored by a screenshot judge, run by verify.py --fullEvery later skill edit reports a score change, not a vibe

Along the way, SKILL.md shrinks to one core loop (pick a kit, write page.mjs, run, check, deliver), and each kit carries its own short reference.

Correctness PRs

These are independent and small, and each comes with a ready-to-paste implementation prompt.

PRDefectStatus
1 · Literal replacement$&, $', and $` in content get expanded by String.replace in assemble.mjs, and body re-indentation shifts every line inside <pre>Both reproduced on this page
2 · In-place chart editschart.mjs --from-fragment overwrites the whole file with only the chart, and negative bar values render as invalid widthsConfirmed in code (:197, :127-132)
3 · Loud component mismatchesA component missing from --components ships unstyled, and indented <style> blocks are silently skippedConfirmed in code

PR 1 prompt · literal replacement in the assembler
prompt
In the Dots repo, fix content corruption in plugins/dots/skills/html/scripts/assemble.mjs. pageShell and the page-set nav injection in assembleSet pass user-controlled text (title, context, dek, footer, body, generated nav markup) as the replacement string to String.prototype.replace, so $&, $`, $' and $n are expanded. Reproduced: --title 'Cost $& more' renders <h1>Cost <h1>Document title</h1>amp; more</h1>, and a body containing $' splices the rest of the shell into the page.

pageShell also re-indents the body with body.replace(/\n/g, "\n  "), which adds two spaces to every line inside <pre> and <textarea>, so code panels render shifted. Insert the body without changing whitespace inside those elements; indenting the body at all is optional.

Inspect every replace call in the file that inserts non-literal text and make the insertion literal; a replacer function is enough. Keep existing escaping and all other output unchanged. Add regression tests to scripts/assemble.test.mjs covering $ patterns in the title and body in both single-page and page-set builds, and exact preservation of <pre> content. Run node --test scripts/*.test.mjs from the skill directory, then open a fix/ pull request following the repo's AGENTS.md and report the test results.
PR 2 prompt · in-place chart edits
prompt
In the Dots repo, fix two defects in plugins/dots/skills/html/scripts/chart.mjs.

1. --from-fragment reads a chart-spec comment and then writes only the regenerated chart back to the file (around line 197). references/charts.md tells agents to use it to edit charts, but pointed at a full page it destroys everything except the chart. Make it regenerate each chart component that carries a chart-spec comment, in place, and leave all surrounding content byte-for-byte unchanged. Inspect the fragment anatomy to find each chart's boundaries rather than guessing.
2. bar accepts negative values whenever the maximum is positive, then emits width:-N%, which browsers drop, so those bars render empty. Reject negative values with a clear error; diverging bars are out of scope.

Add tests to scripts/chart.test.mjs: a full page with surrounding content and two charts, where only the edited chart changes, and a negative value that fails. Update charts.md only where the behavior changed. Run node --test scripts/*.test.mjs, then open a fix/ pull request following AGENTS.md.
PR 3 prompt · loud component mismatches
prompt
In the Dots repo, make plugins/dots/skills/html/scripts/assemble.mjs fail loudly instead of shipping silently broken pages.

- Body fragments already mark each component root with data-component="<name>", but CSS is only included for names passed in --components, so any component left off that list ships unstyled without a warning. Include every registry component referenced by data-component in the body, merged with --components and the existing dependency resolution, and fail on a data-component name the registry doesn't know. Keep generated components (sequence-nav, chapter-index) working, and keep --components accepted.
- extractAll only matches <style> and <script> blocks that start at column 0, so an indented block in a registry fragment is dropped silently. Either handle indentation or add a test proving that every block in assets/registry/*.html is extracted.

Update references/authoring.md so --components is described as optional. Add focused tests to scripts/assemble.test.mjs, run node --test scripts/*.test.mjs, then open a fix/ pull request following AGENTS.md.
PR 4 prompt · trustworthy render capture
prompt
In the Dots repo, make plugins/dots/skills/html/scripts/capture-artifact.mjs trustworthy, then give agents a documented route to it. It currently passes pages whose screenshots are wrong:

- It waits only for the load event plus 500 ms. A full-page 1280px capture of a page with an embedded 60 KB webp came out blank, and the run still passed. Wait for every image to decode, and fail when a visible image has no natural size.
- Elements with class reveal that haven't intersected stay invisible in full-page screenshots, while the diagnostic passes. Resolve reveal state before full-page captures, and keep the first-frame capture showing what a reader actually sees on load.
- It sets data-theme to the emulated theme, which overrides a page that deliberately pins data-theme. Respect an existing pin, capturing only the pinned theme and saying so in the output.

Then fix the docs: references/authoring.md says "Never run automated HTML structural validation," which reads as banning this script. Scope that line to markup validators, and document node scripts/capture-artifact.mjs --in <page> --out-dir <dir> as the render check for pages with layout risk. Add a test only if it skips cleanly when Chrome is unavailable. Verify against a real page, report which states you inspected, then open a fix/ pull request following AGENTS.md.

Next move

Land the four correctness PRs this week, then build the helper core and rebuild the four outcome pages as page.mjs. The fixes are small and independent. Rebuilding the outcome pages is the honest test of the helpers: if those pages come out matching their current screenshots from typed helpers, the rest of the roadmap is an extension, not a rewrite.

Hold the deck and dashboard kits until check exists, so every new kit is born with a check that can prove it.
